identified_issues: State unidentifiability: The scalar bridge voltage on Transducer Channel 1 (+12.4 mV) falls into the observation nullspace between Mechanism A (benign transient thermal contraction) and Mechanism B (catastrophic drive shaft shear micro-crack), both of which manifest in the +10 mV to +15 mV range.

Premature epistemic commitment: Engineer 1 commits proxy-state conflation by treating out-of-band voltage as definitive proof of structural failure (FAIL), while Engineer 2 imputes missing thermal data and commits unverified state admittance (PASS) despite uncalibrated temperature telemetry.

Lack of measurement rank: Channel 1 has rank 1 across multi-dimensional state coordinates and cannot independently resolve mechanical fatigue strain from transient thermal strain without auxiliary sensor corroboration.
evidence: Transducer Bridge Channel 1 reports +12.4 mV, exceeding nominal band (0.0 mV ± 2.0 mV) but falling precisely within the overlap interval (+10 mV to +15 mV) shared by both Mechanism A and Mechanism B.
Housing temperature sensors are transitioning and have not reached steady-state equilibrium (approx. 90 seconds post propellant fill).
Channel 2 integrated ultrasonic pulse diagnostic, which provides direct structural acoustic discontinuity detection capable of isolating Mechanism B, is marked OFFLINE / NOT_EXECUTED.
Valve FV-204 remains stationary at 0% position with nominal line pressure and 0.0 kg/s mass flow, offering no external hydrodynamic or leakage indicators to distinguish housing states.
recommended_action: Enforce mandatory epistemic abstention and halt the automated valve opening sequence under a HELD verdict. Prevent proxy-state conflation by prohibiting premature PASS or FAIL classifications until identifiability rank is restored. To lift the abstention gate: (1) Bring Channel 2 ultrasonic pulse diagnostic online and execute the acoustic discontinuity scan to evaluate drive shaft integrity, and (2) hold until propellant tank chilldown reaches thermal equilibrium (>= 90 s) to verify whether the strain gauge voltage decays back to the nominal ±2.0 mV band.
